issue.issue_text: Whether interim victim compensation in proceedings for anticipatory bail can be imposed as a condition for the same.

facts: The case before the Supreme Court involved an appeal against a lower court's order that had granted anticipatory bail on the condition that the accused pay interim victim compensation.

law.law_text: Section 357 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, governs victim compensation. It allows a court to order compensation only when it imposes a sentence of fine or a sentence of which a fine forms a part, which occurs after a conviction at the conclusion of a trial.
The Supreme Court established the principle that the question of victim compensation cannot form part of bail jurisprudence. Bail proceedings are not money recovery proceedings.

Precedent from 'Dharmesh v. State of Gujarat' confirms that compensation can only be ordered after the conclusion of a trial, and a bail condition requiring a deposit for the victim's heirs cannot be sustained.

application.application_text: The Court applied Section 357 of the CrPC to the issue, reasoning that compensation is linked to the final outcome of a trial and a finding of guilt. Since anticipatory bail is a pre-trial stage, there is no conviction or sentence, making an order for compensation premature and legally impermissible.

The Court reasoned that determining appropriate compensation is impossible at the bail stage, as it requires a final view on whether the alleged offence was committed. Imposing it pre-trial is a "judicial misadventure."

By treating bail as a mechanism for victim compensation, the lower court conflated two distinct legal concepts. The Court reiterated that bail is meant to ensure the accused's presence at trial, not to serve as a pre-emptive recovery proceeding for the victim.

reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that imposing interim victim compensation as a condition for granting anticipatory bail is an infraction of law. The Court held that compensation can only be considered after a trial concludes with a conviction and sentence. Therefore, the condition to pay interim compensation was quashed, and the issue was rejected.

arguments.issue_text: Whether interim victim compensation in proceedings for anticipatory bail can be imposed as a condition for the same.
appellant_arguments: Imposing a condition to deposit compensation for the victim as a prerequisite for bail is unsustainable in law.
Victim compensation, as per Section 357, can only be considered after the conclusion of the trial when a final determination of guilt is made.
There can be no imposition of compensation before the finality of the matter, i.e., pre-trial.

cases.case_name: Udho Thakur and Anr. ETC. v. The State of Jharkhand & Anr.
cases.principle: The question of interim victim compensation cannot form part of the bail jurisprudence.
The question of interim victim compensation cannot form part of the bail jurisprudence.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The question of interim victim compensation cannot form part of bail jurisprudence, as victim compensation is simultaneous with the final determination of the alleged offense and cannot be imposed before the finality of the matter pre-trial.
obiter: Section 357 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides for an order to pay compensation when a court imposes a sentence of fine or a sentence of which fine forms a part. Such compensation is for any loss or injury suffered by a person due to the act for which the accused has been sentenced.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The question of interim victim compensation cannot form part of the bail jurisprudence, as victim compensation is simultaneous with the final view taken in respect of the alleged offence, i.e., whether it was so committed or not, and thus, there is no question of any imposition pre-finality of the matter pre-trial.
legal_tests_applied: A plain reading of Section 357 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shows that an order to pay compensation can only be made when a court imposes a sentence of fine or a sentence of which fine forms a part. Therefore, such compensation can only arise after the conclusion of the trial and a final determination of guilt.
policy_considerations: Bail cannot per se be granted if a person can afford to deposit the money or has the capacity to pay, as bail jurisprudence should be dependent on the nature of the offences, not financial capacity.

Compensation for a victim is a methodology for redemption in cases of offences against the body, but such a compensation can hardly be determined at the stage of grant of bail, before a trial has concluded.
